Scope and authority: reviewed only quality point 06. Read the actual frozen XLSX with openpyxl: Quality Checks row 7 says 'One reasonable reading, and every capability is reachable from the seed, the provided runtime, or the public internet (network is allowed).' Internal Quality Checks row 7 still says 'with no network'; that internal annotation does not override the shipped row, the skill's Delivery profile, or task.toml:22,38 (public network). Frozen quality-checks.md:29-31 asks for requirement reachability and a second reasonable reading. I read the brief, all six public notes, seed, both Dockerfiles, all five dimensions' criteria/prompts, application context, relevant reference implementation and raw golden observations. A read-only SHA256 check matched all 84 frozen task/rules files against manifest.json; the golden functional and prompt hashes equal the frozen manifest entries. No task edits, provider calls, network requests or Docker runs were made.

Runtime and inputs: instruction.md:5 explicitly says 'There isn't a starter app to finish' and asks for authored examples. environment/assets/seed_data.json:3-4 supplies an empty snippets array and no implementation; overview.md:3,7,9 distinguishes examples from shared saved user records. There is no dependency on nonexistent starter files or private credentials. integration.md:3 makes TypeScript/React/Vite optional. Lines 5-11 define node /app/server.js, 0.0.0.0:3000, /app/public/index.html, GET /api/health, DB_PATH, built frontend, no install on launch, and no runtime dependency on retained /assets or /instructions. environment/Dockerfile:1,9-11 supplies Node 22, Express 5.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.4.1; tests/Dockerfile:1-4,16-21 supplies the same runtime. Public development networking permits frontend tooling. solution/app/server.js:2-8,66-88,101-129 and solution/solve.sh:25-26 demonstrate an implementation using those facilities and shipped assets. No external account/backend or inaccessible data is necessary.

Execution scope: behaviour.md:5 distinguishes fresh JS/HTML documents from CSS copying the last successful document, excluding its old scripts/timers/handlers. Lines 7-15 require cancellation, an aggregate five-second budget, later interaction with a completed preview, latest-success rollback (static restoration allowed), and one-based original-source error lines including HTML/asynchronous failures. security.md:3-11 separates allowed app assets from entered snippets' isolation/no-network boundary, supports ordinary source-written code, excludes arbitrary blocking browser-native operations/generated machine code, and expressly refuses eval/Function, WebAssembly, additional workers and dynamic import while accepting those words as text. This is not a promise to interrupt all native operations or an app-wide offline rule. AST instrumentation, isolated browser frames, bounded pending work and inert snapshots are reachable mechanisms; src/runtime.ts:7-33,36-121,124-161,164-200 provides a feasibility witness. This source review is evidence for QC point 06, not permission for the browser-only app judge to inspect submitted source.

Second-reading challenge: I checked the apparent tension between 'five seconds altogether, including its scheduled callbacks' (behaviour.md:9) and keeping a completed preview interactive after idle (line 11). Reading them together excludes an unconditional five-second lifetime for the completed iframe: line 11 expressly permits later clicking or typing. Pending callbacks share the Run's original deadline, while deliberate input after completed work may execute. app_context.md:18 and functional/prompt.md:15-17,152-162,397-409 preserve that distinction. The judge does not require controls to respond during a literal loop, interruption of excluded native operations, or live handlers in restored snapshots. A conforming design may keep the last-good picture visible while a candidate works, block input during pending work, and restore an inert snapshot (behaviour.md:13; app_context.md:18; functional/prompt.md:180,207). These are explicitly accepted alternatives, not false failures. No unresolved second reading affecting the tested behavior survived.

Storage/interface reachability: behaviour.md:25-29 specifies separate New identities, update-in-place Save, exact loaded fields, trimmed/case-sensitive titles, case-insensitive filename dispatch, stale-revision refusal, retained dirty fields and deliberate reload/reapply in both editor directions. integration.md:7 requires browser/process-restart durability. SQLite transactions and browser-held revisions can supply these outcomes without accounts. policy.md:5 leaves layout, labels, indentation, routes and request fields free. ui.md:3-9 requires reachable responsive panes, basic editor features, labelled keyboard controls, visible focus and two themes, while permitting authored preview colours. The grading texts preserve that flexibility: server-rendered library data without a separate JSON endpoint is explicitly accepted in Constraints and the scored gates; Polish P02 permits native/composite menus and ordinary undocumented editor escape keys. Proactive stale-save prevention with exact draft retention remains valid, coupled with independent server stale-request rejection (functional/prompt.md:375-380). No specific recovery button is imposed.

Raw observations independently checked: RESULTS.json facts.S03.later_interactions records click/key/input marker counts of 1 with untouched waits of 6105.016 ms and 6104.580 ms; drivers/runtime_flow.cjs:35-49 actually performs those interactions and Stop. S02.css_pending_timer_cancelled records css-timer-fired-1 before/after CSS, observed css-timer-start-2, and no second fired marker; drivers/current_flow.cjs:18-22 supplies the successful matching timer and cancellation. S36.callback_shared_run_deadline records nested-control-done, then late-callback-entered and 'Execution stopped: five-second time limit', restored nested-control-done and successful recovery. I verified current_flow.cjs:41-48 and run_workflow.cjs dispatch; the older S36 branch in runtime_flow.cjs is not the executed current fixture. S22.process_restart_durability records Primary id 3/revision 2 and Second id 4/revision 1 unchanged across the single restart, PID 16 becoming 335. S23.stale_save_draft_recovery records both editor directions, exact dirty title/filename/source retention, useful conflict messages, and recovery on id 5 through revisions 1 to 5. These are concrete witnesses that the tested lifecycle and shared-library requirements are reachable.

Broken-implementation challenge: destroying every frame five seconds after a successful run fails the explicit later-interaction requirement and S03; giving each nested timer a fresh deadline emits forbidden-nested-completion and fails S36; a dead timer implementation cannot establish cancellation because S02/S04/S36 require observed matching successful callbacks. A static page/browser-only localStorage library cannot supply the authored-execution and independent clean-context retrieval gates. These candidates are broken apps, not conforming alternative readings. No credible false-pass or false-fail witness attributable to instruction ambiguity or environment unreachability survived.

Evidence limits: the golden run is direct pinned Playwright product evidence, not a configured LLM judge run. RESULTS.json states paid_provider=false, browser_driver='direct pinned Playwright', restart_driver='canonical verifier MCP restart_app', wall_seconds=98.02680282300571 and oracle_score_claimed=false. No claim is made about full-judge workload, Oracle grade, target-model score, hosted acceptance or all-QC clearance. Run verdict PARTIAL reflects that relevant product scenarios were observed, not every possible supported source or the full configured evaluation.
